Read the immutable packet's required raw units, exact implementation/test selections, and policy, then inspected the supporting bundled context identified in the rationale. rationale:
unit:meta.evidence.required_inputs requires an independently derived minimum, exact selections as well as full-source context, and current identity for every input. rust:mdbook-dada/src/inventory.rs:Inventory::inputs starts from add_unit, whose complete bundled implementation stores unit.raw, performs kind-specific lean::select for each target, stores each selected declaration under its lean: key, includes exact Rust/test selections and their containing files, and recursively includes :uses: and recognized linked units. Inventory::inputs additionally captures configuration/Cargo metadata, Rust tool sources/tests, renderer Lean fixtures, configured policy/context, and all local Lean sources plus Lake/toolchain metadata when Lean selections are present. The separately required lean: key means an enclosing context file cannot replace the exact declaration.

rust:mdbook-dada/src/evidence.rs:validate_bundle reconstructs that set from inventory.inputs, regenerates extra: files from current project paths, and compares content, hash, and path for every expected key; it reports missing, stale/substituted, and unexpected keys. ReviewBundle::integrity_errors in the full evidence.rs snapshot checks snapshot hashes, manifest digest, duplicate keys, schema, and positive source lines. Inventory::extra_input/file_input/input_path show that extra inputs are actual contained project files, not arbitrary review-supplied content. The missing/substituted-input test independently repacks consistent hashes after dropping authored/selected/dependent/policy/context/Cargo/toolchain inputs and after replacing an exact declaration. Its original full Lean context remains present, so the test directly distinguishes whole-file snapshots from required exact selections. The renderer-fixture test checks fixture capture, deletion from a repacked manifest, and edit-triggered recording/check failure. Changed paths, inconsistent hashes, and the general extra-input branch are supported by inspected implementation beyond those two cited tests.

The required dependent units were also compared in full: meta.units.closed_body's parse_block/validate_chapters reject expansion and compare original/processed raw units; meta.sources.configuration shares SourceConfiguration and project-root Rust selection; meta.sources.exact_selection preserves complete constructor/member text and rejects unsupported sibling/mutual commands. Their selected tests cover nested citations, preexpanded and actual mdBook input, moved source roots, final literal tokens, mutual members/decoys, and malformed mutual groups. The corresponding helper portions of units.rs, lib.rs, lean.rs, and test fixtures were inspected to connect those selections to the inventory boundary.

The terminology is established in the bundled authoring guide and spec-system.md's opening, Evidence and validation, and Selecting formalizations sections: units have IDs/raw bodies, citations select source, and bundles/records preserve inputs/decisions. This implementation contract uses ordinary prose and code identifiers rather than mathematical metavariables; no undefined judgment or forward mathematical reference is needed.
limitations: This is a source correspondence review. I inspected the cited test bodies and their fixtures but did not execute Cargo, mdBook, or Lean in this review; it supplies no mechanical pass claim.

For conservative snapshots, examined records use of the relevant portions, not a claim to have audited every line. I read spec-system.md lines 1-217 and 282-385; supporting Rust/test portions are identified in the rationale. Unrelated renderer features and Lean proof bodies were not reviewed.
The included actual_mdbook_pipeline_rejects_includes_in_reviewed_content test is explicitly ignored by default and needs an installed mdbook plus a separate --ignored run; I did not run it.

The two tests cited directly by this unit demonstrate selected missing/substituted and renderer-fixture cases. Path substitution, raw hash corruption, and extra-input generality are supported here by source inspection. This review does not turn syntactic freshness into mathematical correspondence or elaborated Lean dependency tracking.
